questions.question: What is the specificity weight of the :where() pseudo-class?
options: It matches the highest argument
It always has strictly zero specificity (0, 0, 0, 0)
It has the specificity of an ID
It has the specificity of a class
questions.explanation: :where() always has zero specificity (0,0,0,0), regardless of how specific its arguments are.

questions.question: How is the specificity of :is(h1, .lead, #hero) calculated?
options: It evaluates to zero
It takes the specificity of its most specific argument, which is the ID #hero (0, 1, 0, 0)
It sums all three selectors together
It defaults to a class weight
questions.hint: Takes the highest specificity in the list.
questions.explanation: :is() adopts the specificity of the most specific selector in its argument list (the ID in this case).

questions.question: Which pseudo-class allows styling an element based on the presence of certain children or siblings?
options: :has()
:parent()
:contains()
:matches()
questions.explanation: :has() represents an element if any of the selectors passed as an argument matches at least one element relative to it.

questions.question: Why is :where() extensively used in modern CSS resets and framework libraries?
options: It compresses file size
Its zero specificity allows consumers to easily override library styles with a simple single-class rule
It bypasses HTML validation
It only applies in dark mode
questions.hint: Easy overrides due to zero specificity.
questions.explanation: Because :where() has 0 specificity, developers can override library defaults effortlessly without specificity conflicts.

questions.question: What happens if a selector passed into :is() is invalid (e.g. :is(h1, :invalid-selector))?
options: The entire CSS stylesheet fails
The browser ignores only the invalid item and applies the rule to the valid selectors (forgiving selector list)
The browser throws an error alert
The page turns blank
questions.explanation: :is() and :where() use forgiving selector lists: invalid selectors are safely ignored without breaking the remaining valid ones.
